teams.heading: Fiji defeat Canada to secure Pacific Nations Cup final spot against Japan
teams.body: Defending champions Fiji have advanced to the Pacific Nations Cup final after defeating Canada. This victory sets up a title-deciding clash against Japan, keeping the Flying Fijians on track to retain their regional crown. The result provides a timely boost for the squad as they build momentum towards their upcoming northern hemisphere fixtures, with the final against the Brave Blossoms now representing their immediate focus.

lead.why: Fiji have defeated Canada to reach the Pacific Nations Cup final against Japan, keeping their title defence alive.

teams.heading: Ben Youngs accuses Bill Sweeney of having 'blinkers on' over Steve Borthwick
teams.body: Former England scrum-half Ben Youngs has criticised RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney and performance director Conor O’Shea for their continued support of Steve Borthwick. Despite what O’Shea described as a "horrendous" Six Nations campaign, Borthwick has been handed a contract extension through to the 2028 championship. Youngs claimed the governing body has "blinkers on" regarding the head coach’s 59.6% win rate. While Borthwick guided England to two wins from three during the summer, Youngs warned that the executive duo remain "accountable" if form dips before next year’s World Cup.

lead.why: The vocal criticism from England’s most-capped male player regarding the head coach's job security is the most significant talking point in today’s domestic coverage.

Les Bleus currently hold a strong position in the tournament log, having secured 2 wins from their opening 3 matches to sit 3rd in the standings with a points difference of +41 following their recent 42-15 success over Japan.

teams.heading: IRFU Dismisses Plans to Host Six Nations Fixtures in United States
teams.body: The Irish Rugby Football Union has ruled out moving any Six Nations matches to the United States. Following comments from World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin, who suggested that fixtures involving Ireland could resonate with American-based expatriate fans, the IRFU released a statement on Friday. The union confirmed there are "currently no plans or discussions" regarding such a move, reiterating that maintaining home matches in Ireland remains a central component of the competition’s appeal for their supporters.

lead.why: The IRFU has issued an official statement clarifying its position on the future of Six Nations fixtures.

teams.heading: Rhea Clarke and Evie Gallagher return for Scotland’s Canada WXV opener
teams.body: Scrum-half Rhea Clarke makes her first start for Scotland as the team opens their WXV Series campaign against Canada in Edinburgh. Interim head coach Dave Butcher has also recalled flanker Evie Gallagher, who joins captain Rachel Malcolm in the back row for her first appearance since last year’s World Cup. Despite the sudden departure of former head coach Sione Fukofuka, fly-half Helen Nelson insists the squad’s transition has been "seamless" as they look to improve upon last year’s World Cup performance.

teams.heading: Ben Carter cleared to resume competitive rugby with the Dragons
teams.body: Wales lock Ben Carter is fully recovered from the ankle injury that ruled him out of the mid-July defeat to South Africa. Having avoided surgery, the 25-year-old is now fit and training ahead of his club’s United Rugby Championship opener. Dragons defence coach Dale MacLeod noted that Carter is in excellent condition, stating: "It's not an issue now. He is going really well and is probably in the best nick that I have seen him."

lead.why: The report clarifies Ben Carter's availability following his injury-enforced absence from the summer Tests.

teams.heading: Wallabies legend James Slipper pauses career for new Brumbies coaching role
teams.body: Veteran front-rower James Slipper has been appointed as the Brumbies’ scrum coach on a temporary basis, marking a shift in his professional focus. The 154-Test veteran, who remains under contract with the club for another season, will step away from on-field duties during Super Rugby AUS to join Stephen Larkham’s coaching staff. Slipper aims to share lessons from his extensive career with the squad’s emerging forwards, filling the vacancy left by John Ulugia’s recent move to the national set-up.

lead.why: The transition of the most capped international prop in history into a coaching role is a significant development for Australian rugby's forward development.

teams.body: Coach Dave Rennie has reshuffled the All Blacks lineup for the final Test in Baltimore, headlined by the return of Richie Mo’unga at fly-half. Following a 29-24 victory in the third Test, the Springboks have secured wins in the second and third encounters. Rassie Erasmus has confirmed changes to the starting line-up for the fourth Test in Baltimore, with Damian Willemse replacing the injured Cheslin Kolbe and Morne van den Berg coming in at scrum-half to face the All Blacks.
